content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.3) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for consecutive high sentiment days.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (forecast overshoots true value by >10%) — apply downward correction of 5–15% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Model tends to overreact to recent highs — dampen forecast peaks by 10–20% if sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Forecast horizon error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) — reduce first 5 forecast points by 5–10% if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- Sentiment decay effect: if sentiment drops below 0.15 over 3 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 3–7% to reflect weakening momentum.
